title: Minced Tissue in Compressed Collagen: A Cell-containing Biotransplant for Single-staged Reconstructive Repair
protocol: Prepare the surgical table with all materials and instruments needed for the operation under sterile conditions.
Fast the animal for 12 hr prior to surgery and measure its weight.
Administer an intramuscular injection of azaperone (2 mg/kg) for premedication.
Anesthetize the animal with intramuscular injections of tiletamine hypochloride (2.5 mg/kg), zolazepam hypochloride (2.5 mg/kg), medetomidine (25 µg/kg), and atropine (25 µg/kg).
Inject phenobarbiturate (15 mg/kg) prior to endotracheal intubation.
Continue general anesthesia with 0.8%–2% isoflurane during the procedure.
Insert a peripheral vein catheter in one ear.
Infuse glucose (25 mg/ml) intravenously during the procedure to maintain well-being of the animal.
Place monitoring devices on the ear or tail to check temperature, blood pressure, saturation, and peripheral pulse.
Control anesthesia by pain stimulation of the ears or hooves.
Apply ointment to eyes to prevent dryness while under anesthesia.

Catheterize the bladder using a 10-French silicone catheter by introducing a speculum to view the urethra and inserting the catheter through the urethra into the urinary bladder under semi-sterile conditions.
Empty the urine from the bladder.
Fill the bladder with sterile saline solution to a pressure of 20–25 cm H2O, approximately 100–300 ml.
Reduce the volume in the bladder to maintain a pressure of about 20 cm H2O (approximately 8 ml/kg of body weight).
Turn the pig carefully into a side position.
Sterilize the skin with chlorhexidine gluconate under semi-sterile conditions.
Remove pelage from the shoulder area using shaving shears.
Apply a diathermy plate to the shoulder after removing the pelage.
Turn the pig carefully into a supine position.
Remove abdominal pelage using shaving shears.
Sterilize the abdominal skin with chlorhexidine gluconate under semi-sterile conditions.
Embed the extremities with soft clothing to minimize hyperextension damage to joints.
Apply sterile draping around the surgical field.
Apply an intravenous analgesic consisting of buprenorphine (45 µg/kg), carprofen (3 mg/kg) and local injection of lidocaine in the midline below the umbilicus.
Check for pain reaction by grasping the skin with forceps.
Make a lower midline incision through the fascia and peritoneum using diathermy for control of bleeding.
Localize the bladder, which has a fully intraperitoneal position in the pig and can be freely exposed by mobilizing it through the surgical wound.
Take hold of the bladder with the forceps.
Measure the bladder with a sterilized measuring tape.
Mark an elliptic-shaped biopsy specimen approximately 2 cm longitudinally and 1 cm transversally, or smaller, using a sterilized pen.
Excise the marked area using a scalpel.
Place the bladder biopsy specimen in DMEM under sterile conditions.
Prepare the surgical table with all necessary materials.
Anesthetize the animal as previously described in section 1.1.
Remove the pelage using wax.
Wash and sterilize the incision area with betadine and 70% alcohol.
Place sterile draping around the incision area.
Use a dermatome to harvest a 0.3 mm partial thickness skin biopsy specimen.
Place the skin specimen in DMEM before mincing, as described in section 2.2.
Cover the wound area with fatty ointment and a dressing.
Close the bladder by suturing it with 5-0 Vicryl in two layers.
Close the abdominal fascia carefully with 2-0 or 3-0 running Vicryl.
Close the subcutis with 3-0 Vicryl and the skin with 3-0 Ethilon.
Place a dressing on the wound.
Attend to the animal until it has recovered sufficiently from the anesthesia and does not express pain.
Move the animal to the animal care facility to secure conditions for postoperative care.
Put the animal in a single cage with a heating lamp.
Administer buprenorphine (45 μg/kg) intramuscularly for postoperative analgesia.
Administer trimetoprim (4 mg/kg) and sulfonamide (20 mg/kg) twice daily for three days and once daily for five days to reduce the risk of postoperative infections.
Wash the bladder biopsy twice in DMEM.
Place the bladder biopsy specimen onto a sterilized dissecting plate with the mucosa facing upwards.
Fix one side of the bladder biopsy to the plate using dissection pins.
Separate the mucosal tissue from the detrusor muscle using fine scissors and forceps.
Keep the mucosa moist by dripping saline or DMEM over it.
Use the mincing device by placing it on the mucosa.
Pass the device from one end to the other vertically and horizontally, applying manual pressure.
Obtain pieces of minced tissue measuring 0.8 mm x 0.8 mm.
If the skin biopsy is thick: place the skin onto a sterile dissecting plate.
Separate the epidermis from subcutaneous fat and dermis using surgical scissors.
Place the mincing device on the epidermis.
Pass the device from one end to the other vertically and horizontally with pressure.
Obtain pieces of minced tissue measuring 0.8 mm x 0.8 mm.
Prepare all ingredients on ice to keep them cold for making plastic compressed PCL/collagen autografts.
Mix 2 ml of 10x DMEM carefully to avoid bubbles.
Add 12 ml of collagen type 1.
Drop by drop, add 1 N NaOH to bring pH up to 7.4–8 (indicated by a change from intense yellow to pink).
Use a pH strip to verify the pH.
Carefully add 2 ml of 1x DMEM and mix the solution.
Plate approximately 2 ml of collagen in each well of the steel rectangular mold.
Incubate at 37 °C in 5% CO2 for 10 min.
Pour remaining collagen (about 6 ml) on top of the PCL biomaterial placed on a set collagen gel.
Incubate at 37 °C in 5% CO2 for 20 min.
Place a thick layer of gauze pads on a sterile surface.
Place one stainless steel mesh on top of the gauze pads and then a sheet of nylon mesh.
Carefully transfer the collagen gel/minced tissue onto the nylon mesh.
Remove the rectangular steel mold carefully.
Place another layer of nylon mesh on top of the collagen gel/minced tissue.
Place a second steel mesh on top of the nylon mesh.
Place in position the pressure or loading plate weighing at least 120 g for 5 min.
Remove the weight, nylon, and steel meshes.
Cut the thin construct into small pieces fitting 12-well plates for in vitro culturing.
Add 1 ml of keratinocyte medium to each well.
Place the plates in the incubator at 37 °C with 5% CO2.
Culture up to 6 weeks.
Change the medium 3 times per week.
Keep the autograft moist in DMEM during the waiting time for suture.
Suture the autograft with fine running monofilament sutures using non-absorbable 5-0 Ethilon.
Check if watertight by filling the bladder with saline through the indwelling urinary catheter.
Cover the autograft with a layer of greater omentum if possible.
Close the abdominal wall, subcutaneous tissue, and skin as described in 1.2.6.
Apply a wound dressing after suturing.
Keep the autograft moist in DMEM during the waiting time for suture to full-thickness wounds.
Suture the autograft to the bottom of the skin full-thickness wound by interrupted sutures in the corners and middle.
Cover the wound with a plastic dressing that keeps the wound moist.
Sedate the animal with an intramuscular injection of zolazepam hypochloride (2.5 mg/kg) and medetomidine (25 µg/kg).
Apply monitoring devices to the ear or tail to check for pulse and blood pressure.
Euthanize the animal by administering a lethal dose of pentobarbital sodium (60-140 mg/kg) intravenously.
Check pulse and blood pressure until death has occurred.
Sterilize a 500 ml glass bottle.
Mix 400 ml of DMEM with 100 ml of Ham’s F12 medium (4:1 mixture).

Supplement the mixture with 10% fetal bovine serum, 5 µg/ml insulin, 0.4 µg/ml hydrocortisone, 21 µg/ml adenine, 10-10 mol/L cholera toxin, 2 x 10-9 mol/L triiodothyronine, 5 µg/ml transferrin, 10 ng/ml epidermal growth factor, 50 U/ml penicillin, and 50 µg/ml streptomycin.
Sterilize the solution by filtering through a 0.2 μm filter.
Collect the filtrate in the sterile 500 ml bottle.
Prepare Eppendorf tubes with 1 ml of 4% buffered formaldehyde (PFA).
Transfer each of the collagen patches to an Eppendorf tube containing 4% PFA.
Fix over night at room temperature.
Place samples in 70% ethanol for long-term storage at 4 °C.
Place the slides in a staining jar with X-tra solv for 15 min.
Repeat by using a new staining jar with X-tra solv.
Place the slides in a staining jar with absolute ethanol for 10 min.
Repeat by using a new staining jar with absolute ethanol.
Place the slides in a staining jar with 95% ethanol for 10 min.
Place the slides in a staining jar with 70% ethanol for 10 min.
Wash the slides twice for 5 min with distilled water.
Put slides in a Coplin jar with TE-solution and put the jar in a water bath to boil for 20 min.
Take the jar out of the water bath carefully.
Cool the slides to room temperature for 30 min.
Wash the slides twice for 5 min in Tris buffer.
Place the slides in a staining jar with 3% hydrogen peroxide for 10 min.
Wash the slides twice for 5 min in Tris buffer.
Draw a circle around the samples using a water repellent marking pen.
Block nonspecific binding of the antibody using 100–300 µl of blocking solution.
Remove the blocking solution and add 100–300 µl of primary antibody dissolved at the recommended concentration in Tris buffer.
Incubate overnight.
Remove the antibody solution and wash sections in Tris buffer twice for 5 min.
Incubate with the secondary antibody for 1 hr at room temperature.
Wash the slides twice for 5 min in Tris buffer.
Incubate 30 min using the ABC Elite Kit (follow the manufacturer’s instructions).
Wash the slides twice in Tris buffer.
Develop antibody reaction using the Vector VIP Kit as per manufacturer’s instructions.
Put the slides in distilled water.
Counterstain with Mayer’s hematoxylin for 30 seconds.
Wash the slides in running water for 5 minutes.
Place the slides in a staining jar with 70% ethanol for 1 minute.
Repeat by using a new staining jar with 70% ethanol.
Place the slides in a staining jar with 95% ethanol for 1 minute.
Repeat by using a new staining jar with 95% ethanol.
Place the slides in a staining jar with X-tra solv for 5 minutes.
Remove the slides one at a time to keep them moist.
Place a drop of mounting medium on top of each slide and put a cover glass on top carefully to avoid air bubbles.
Let the slides dry overnight.
